messages:
Sam Kapoor: hey team — first week! trying to get the local stack running (postgres + redis) per the README. running `docker-compose -f infra/compose/local.yml up` and postgres keeps crashing with this error:

Sam Kapoor: ```postgres_1 | initdb: data directory "/var/lib/postgresql/data" has wrong ownership
postgres_1 | initdb: removing contents of data directory "/var/lib/postgresql/data"
postgres_1 | chown: changing ownership of '/var/lib/postgresql/data': Operation not permitted
```

Sam Kapoor: also redis immediately exits with `bind: address already in use` — I think I might have a local redis on my mac? on M1 Macbook Pro (macOS 13). any tips for the right compose bits or env vars? @Maya @Oliver

Maya Lin (devex): welcome Sam! :tada: common things: on macs the file permissions / bind mounts can cause that postgres ownership error. are you mounting a host folder to `/var/lib/postgresql/data` in the compose file or using a named volume?

Sam Kapoor: I'm mounting `./dev/db/pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data` because the README asked to persist.

Maya Lin (devex): ok — that's the culprit. Docker on mac (esp with gRPC FUSE vs osxfs) can make chown fail inside the container. two options that work reliably:
1) switch to a named docker volume (recommended): in compose set `volumes: - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data` and add `volumes:
  pgdata:` at bottom. then run `docker compose down -v && docker compose up` to recreate.
2) if you really need host bind, `sudo chown -R 999:999 dev/db/pgdata` (999 is postgres uid in the image) — but only if you're comfortable changing ownership.

Maya Lin (devex): also check the image tag — use `postgres:14-bullseye` (no alpine) for better compatibility on arm64. example snippet:
```yaml
services:
  postgres:
    image: postgres:14-bullseye
    environment:
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: localdev
    volumes:
      - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data

volumes:
  pgdata:
```

Oliver Chen: re: redis — that "address already in use" usually means you have a brew-installed redis running. run `lsof -i :6379` or `brew services list`. if it's running, either `brew services stop redis` or change compose port mapping to `6379:6379` -> `6380:6379` locally.

Sam Kapoor: nice — I do have redis from brew. Stopping it fixed the crash. For postgres, switched to a named volume and `docker compose down -v` then up. still see `permission denied` on first init attempt, but second `docker compose up` worked.

Maya Lin (devex): yep first init can leave a bad dir. if you hit weird state run:
```
docker compose down -v
docker volume prune  # or `docker volume rm <repo>_pgdata`
# then docker compose up
```

Sam Kapoor: quick followups: do we have a helper script to run migrations and seed local data? README mentions `make local` but I'm getting `make: *** No rule to make target 'local'.`

Oliver Chen: there is a script under `scripts/setup_local_db.sh` and a make target `make dev` in the root that runs the compose + migrations. in your branch the Makefile might be different. try `./scripts/setup_local_db.sh` then `poetry run alembic upgrade head` (python stack) or `npm run migrate` if you're on the node service.

Sam Kapoor: ran `./scripts/setup_local_db.sh` — it prompted for DB password and then applied migrations. all green now. thanks!

Lisa (infra): FYI if you see slow filesystem IO on Docker Desktop, enable "Use gRPC FUSE" in Docker Desktop settings — better perf for mounts on mac. also if images pull as amd64 on M1, add `platform: linux/arm64` to service or use multi-arch images.

Sam Kapoor: thanks everyone! leaving notes in my onboarding doc for next hires about the pgdata -> named volume tip and brew redis conflict. :+1:

Devex-Bot: Reminder: post your resolved onboarding issues in #new-hires-onboarding so we can add to the checklist.
